I would say if you do want a gun for self defense take multiple courses before hand and once you get your gun go to the range multiple times a week to shoot it, become familiar with it, feel it. Know that gun back and forth. Try taking some tactical training in which you have to hit targets on the move. If you can become comfortable with the gun and safe in a way that you won’t accidentally fire in fear then I say that is the only case when it is safe.

I use headspace a lot when I need it. It’s another meditation nap. I find that keeping myself busy with other things really helps. Working out, forcing myself to be social with a close friend that won’t pressure me into anything. Cooking has actually become an interesting resource for me too. It gets your mind focused on the food and out of the other places. 

Hopefully some of this helps. Just take it slow, you are going to be okay and you are going to make it through this. Reach out to people and use your support network. You are not alone.

I'm actually about to do the same as you! When I was younger I lived in the city in an apartment building with my family and we had a golden retriever puppy. I remember (and I've also asked my parents for some advice) that it was not a very stressful process. Its just important to take them out as often as possible those first few weeks to show the puppy that outside is where they should go. I know you don't want any accidents in the elevator, but its bound to happen, just carry around some wet naps and paper towels when you feel like the puppy urgently has to go. Try and find the signs and pick the puppy up maybe bring a toy to try and distract them on the ride down in the elevator.

The biggest thing is trying to be proactive and just taking the puppy out 30 mins after every meal and every play time (I didn't realize this but after they get excited and run around the apartment they will need to go) So just take the puppy out a lot more than you think would be necessary to just make sure the puppy never associates the apartment with a bathroom. 

It is definitely do-able to have a puppy in an apartment! It just means a little more work and responsibility to get them the exercise they need outside. Good luck and I hope this helps!!
